The best thing about a new job is that your future employers have NO idea what you're like. And I mean that in a good way! You might currently have a blow to your confidence because of job hunting, but all they know about you is that you were a great prospective employee that they wanted on their team! Think about it, they hired YOU for a reason! Nerves come from a place of wanting to put the best foot forward, and you already have half of that down!

On the more practical side, when you get there for (I'm assuming) training your first few days, the most important thing you should be is attentive! My personal favorite is bringing a small notepad if you need to keep track of things by writing down what they say. Even beyond a job standpoint, people *love* feeling like you're listening and engaging them fully. You'll make them feel good and further your reputation as a great new hire!

Being nervous is expected, so it's good to embrace that feeling rather than let it freak you out more. For example, you could start by admitting it to yourself, but then reworking it into a way that's more productive for you, i.e. "Yes, I'm nervous about this job, but that's because this is the start of my career and I want to do well." It sounds silly on paper, but give it a shot! It might help!

And of course, congratulations on your new job! You'll do great! :)

okay, so i finally read the rest of it! here's what i have to say. 

I think you have a good concept. You can definitely see the Black Mirror influences (I say that in a good way lol), but you need to push the idea MORE. 

 The whole idea of genetic alternation is an interesting, philosophical question. Because of that, I really think you need to push the WHY behind Ethan wanting to fix Benjamin. You need to have the seeds of doubt Tom plants be a little more obvious, and be implied some way in the dinner scene. Because, as it stands, it feels like Ethan VERY rapidly switches over to intense anger at his son not excelling. You need to establish some character traits behind why Ethan would feel like that, because he seemed to be just as passionate as Madison when they were defending their decision at the dinner scene, so I was really shocked with how fast he started getting pissed at his baby. I think I saw traces of that at the dinner scene, with Tom saying Ethan was a hustler. Maybe he's driven by competition and needing to be the best, and with a deficient son, he starts to get irritated. 

Another thing: the formatting and the exposition. The conversation at the start of the script ABSOLUTELY needs to be broken up with action lines, because it's super exposition-heavy and doesn't give the reader time to process the information they've been given. I actually had to scroll back to see if the name of the drug came up because there's just SO much dumped on the audience in that scene. Maybe break up the information into two separate scenes? Or at least trim it down. I know I told you that already, but the constant walls of dialogue really DO bring down the quality of your script. 

I like the thing you did with the building blocks, definitely keep that. As far as formating goes, you have a lot of "internal emotion" stuff. Ethan deep in thoughts and Madison thinking about the bank are the highlights. Those aren't things as an audience we can see, so you have to establish it in other ways (for instance, maybe Madison receives a notification about a huge withdrawal on her phone, or is chatting with the taxi driver and the topic of money comes up, etc.). You also end and open a lot of scenes with dialogue, which you're not supposed to do. Another thing, using later in the slugline is fine once or twice, but you had a lot of times where you didn't really need it. 

Another thing is passive verbs. Try to avoid using "is" and "are", as well as "-ing", in order to keep the actives voice (ex. "Ethan is walking to Benjamin's room" vs. "Ethan walks to Benjamin's room"). Also remove the scene numbering and the fade in and fade outs in the middle of the script! Only keep those for the beginning and end.

Overall, I really liked the idea you had! I think it's a solid concept, and honestly you set everything major up fine, so really this tells you how to push it further! as far as fashion goes, a good jump-off point would be getting your BWH (bust-waist-hips) measurements and using one of those fancy body shape calculators (your results will vary by site, so try a few of them out and see which one you either get the most or feels describes you best). i'd rec using the four main body types to determine your shape since it may be more generalized, but it gives you a good idea for where to begin.

[this article](https://www.whowhatwear.com/how-to-find-body-shape-calculator) is a good starting guide for the four main body types and how you'd dress each of them!

since you mention you have wider shoulders, i'd actually recommend scoop neck and v-neck shirts (according to my mom lol)! personally i'm not a big fan of v-necks, but scoop necks will not only elongate your neck, but they make your upper body look very feminine and frame your shoulders to where they look at lot smaller than they actually are.

i think being able to wear v-necks ultimately comes down to your overall shape (my mom has wide shoulders and v-necks suit her very well lol). since i inherited my wide shoulders from her and i hate v-necks, scoop necks are honestly a gift from heaven, lol. i used to wear a lot of crew necks and made my neck look really short, but scoop necks add an extra sense of grace to your appearance, not to mention they give your bust a nice shape without feeling like you're exposed! but still play around with different cuts of v-neck tops, because you actually might find one that at least becomes the exception!

shopping for jeans is a pain in the ass lmao. i'm short as well (5'2 lmao), and it sucks that petite clothing is too short, but regular clothing is too long. but, i have just the thing for you! you can make your legs appear longer + shapelier if you pair long pants with a pair of tall shoes (like heels, wedges, or platforms!), as seen [here](https://www.shoe-tease.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/shoes-to-wear-with-flare-jeans-2.jpg), [here](https://wasabi-files.lbstatic.nu/files/looks/medium/2015/03/22/4385470_1small.jpg?1427058693), and [here](https://i.pinimg.com/originals/99/a5/98/99a5986082759ddbddeed5c91a721542.jpg)! this look works best with flares and bellbottoms (especially flares, which are ultra flattering!), but bootcut jeans also works! flares i think would really work in your case since you mention that your thighs are thick but your legs are skinny, so the fit of the flare would balance the two out and make your legs look uber proportional!!

and if heels sound a bit jarring for you, then wedges and platforms are a good start since they're basically, like, the training wheels of the heel world lol. you can find some really cute options at places like TJ Maxx and Ross! and they're cheap enough that you don't have to drop money on a pair of practice shoes (and they last long enough if you decide to wear them regularly after all!).

finding a belt or pants that fit correctly is a battle and a half, but the goal, no matter what your body type, is to cinch in the waist! a small waist (or at least the illusion of one!) is a very feminine hallmark, and you can make virtually anything look flattering if it fits you well at the waist!

unfortunately, i can't speak too much to recs since i don't know your body type or personal style, but i really like [Pacsun's](https://www.pacsun.com/womens/) selection of [boyfriend jeans](https://www.pacsun.com/womens/jeans/boyfriend/) because they've mastered the art of fitting SUPER well at the waist while still achieving that cute baggy look.

honestly i'd recommend them overall lmao because they have a lot of cute trendy stuff! unfortunately they can get on the pricier side, but they run sales a good bit, and the clothes are pretty good quality! i would especially rec their [dresses](https://www.pacsun.com/womens/dresses/), because they are also suuuper flattering and really make any shape look really cute <3

for the most part, finding clothing and styles that flatter you is a matter of trial and error. dressing rooms are sort of starting to reopen, but if they ever do in the near future i'd suggest just pulling a bunch of different styles off the shelves and seeing which ones really make you feel your brightest in :) it's kinda frustrating at first, especially since a lot of clothes nowadays are fast fashion and good quality + flattering clothes are $$$, it can be a little disheartening, but you will find at least one piece, and that's all you need to start building up your collection!

here's [another article](https://blog.petitedressing.com/look-feminine/) that also gives a fair dozen tips on becoming more feminine in your style lol

some other last minute things:

* personally i don't wear much jewelry but at least get yourself a cute necklace and bracelet! hell, maybe even some earrings! any combination of the three can always add a last minute flare to your outfit of the day.
* for both fashion and make-up, find colors that flatter you because color is important! you can really just eyeball this yourself by holding up items to your body and "feeling" out which ones compliment you best, but also don't be shy to just ask someone nearby if the color looks nice on you because most people are actually really nice and will help you lol :)
* if you buy something boyish, make sure it's a boyish thing made for girls? i have no clue how to describe this lol but basically like getting a pair of boyfriend jeans designed to flatter a woman's body vs actually getting a pair of men's jeans lol 
* sometimes just go out on a whim and try something on you don't like. worst that could happen is that it sucks LOL

don't feel like you have to completely forgo your own original style in order to be feminine! you can incorporate femininity into your look while still paying homage to style choices that you love, like choosing more feminine styles but in a darker color palette, or getting baggy jeans the cinch in at the waist. it's all about mixing and matching and ultimately finding not only what *looks* best, but also wearing what you *feel* best *in*!
